next_step: Finalize Dedicated sizing + submit procurement PO; pricing review call 2026-03-15
notes:
Brief: Mid-market product company building an in-app intelligent support assistant + contextual doc search. Started with Hosted API POC to validate latency and quality; now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. Key pain: token costs at scale and unpredictable latency spikes during high-concurrency windows. Cost workshop run with Redwood SE on 2026-02-28 covering batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles.

POC summary:
- Dataset: 150k docs (help center + README + release notes) indexed; embeddings baseline on hosted API (ada-like open model).
- POC traffic target: 30 concurrent chat sessions, avg 2.2 requests/session, target 95p latency < 250ms for short chat turns.
- Throughput requirement: ~250 qps for embeddings rerank jobs during nightly batch windows.

Cost workshop highlights (from SE notes):
- Suggested batching config (dynamic batching with 64 token budget) reduced average token cost by ~22% in POC runs.
- KV/prefix caching expected to lower per-turn compute for repeat user sessions by 35-50% depending on session length.
- Quantization recommendation: 4-bit QKV path for their selected open model variant yields ~2.6x throughput uplift with minor quality checks. Redwood proposed custom quant profile for their model family.
- Unit economics model shared (spreadsheet link) showing break-even at ~40k monthly active users with Dedicated reserved capacity (12mo).

Customer quotes/notes from calls:
- "We like the hosted speed for fast iteration, but need predictable bills for production." — Head of Product (Ava Morris).
- Security lead: requires SOC2 + in-region residency for EU customers; looking at Private for certain enterprise customers but Dedicated may be acceptable if VPC + KMS.

Open items: dry-run of quantized model on their regression prompts, finalize batching policy for live traffic, integration test for KV cache invalidation on content updates.

Links: drive deck + cost model referenced in timeline. Shorthand follow-up items added to next_step.
